intended_object: The identity isogeny id_E : E → E of a Weierstrass curve over a field. In this library's contravariant model it is the pullback F[E] → F(E) given by the canonical embedding of the coordinate ring into the function field (inferred from the docstring and the module documentation).
explanation:
In this library, `Isogeny W₁ W₂` is an F-algebra map from the target coordinate ring to the source function field, together with the condition that every source coordinate function is integral over the target ring acting through that map. This is the algebraic way of saying the map sends the point at infinity to the point at infinity. `Isogeny.id W` takes as its pullback `CoordinatePullback.id W`, which is `IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F W.CoordinateRing W.FunctionField`. By `id_apply`, that map is exactly `algebraMap W.CoordinateRing W.FunctionField`, the canonical embedding of the coordinate ring into its fraction field. This is the pullback along the identity morphism. The integrality condition holds trivially, since each `algebraMap x` is integral over the coordinate ring. So the definition is the identity morphism in this model.

The generality is right. The ambient `Isogeny` structure is stated over any field F, which is the standard setting for isogenies of Weierstrass curves. Mathlib has no notion of isogeny, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
